originalTitle: Oil prices rally, US data dents chances of Fed rate hike
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: oil prices went up because of tensions between countries, which can affect the global economy. At the same time, people in the US are feeling less confident about spending money because everyday costs are rising, and this is hurting sales for some companies. This news is making it less likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon. As a result, the overall stock market is down, especially for companies that make computer chips. This matters because it can impact the value of investments and the overall health of the economy.

originalTitle: Independence Day 2026: How Sensex skyrocketed 8,500% in less than 35 years since 1991 liberalisation reforms
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market, measured by the Sensex, has seen an incredible increase of 8,500% since 1991. This means that if you had invested money in the stock market back then, your investment would be 85 times bigger today. The Sensex has been growing at a rate of about 14% per year, which is a very strong performance. This growth happened even though there were many challenges and problems in the market over the years, such as scandals and global crises. The fact that the Sensex has done so well over time is a significant achievement and shows the strength of the Indian stock market.

originalTitle: Svatantra Microfin files draft papers for Rs 3,000 crore IPO
simplifiedContent: Svatantra Microfin, a company that provides small loans, wants to raise money by selling its shares to the public for the first time, which is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The company plans to raise 3,000 crore rupees, with 1,500 crore coming from selling new shares and the other 1,500 crore from existing investors selling some of their shares. Two big investors, Advent International and Multiples, will be reducing their ownership in the company. The money raised will be used to strengthen the company's finances and help it grow. The company currently has assets worth 21,093 crore rupees, and this IPO is a way for it to get more funds to achieve its goals.

originalTitle: 15 Nifty 500 stocks that doubled investors’ money since last Independence Day: Do you own any?
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: even though the Indian stock market had a tough year, with the main Nifty 50 index going down 2%, some stocks did very well. In fact, 15 stocks in the bigger Nifty 500 index more than doubled in value over the past year, since the last Independence Day. This means that if you invested money in these stocks, your investment would be worth at least twice as much now. It's interesting to note that these stocks were able to perform well despite problems in the world and in the economy. These 15 stocks are considered "stellar" performers and it might be worth checking if you own any of them.

originalTitle: RVNL vs IRFC vs IRCON vs IRCTC: Which railway stock to buy after Q1 results 2026?
simplifiedContent: Some companies that work with the railway system in India just released their quarterly results for 2026. Experts are now comparing these companies, called RVNL, IRFC, IRCON, and IRCTC, to decide which one is a good investment. IRFC is considered a strong choice because it has the support of the government and is involved in big railway projects. RVNL and IRCON are similar because they work on building and constructing railway projects, while IRCTC is unique because it has no competitors in its field. This matters because investors want to know which of these companies is the best to put their money into after seeing their recent performance.

originalTitle: Stocks to buy under  ₹200: Mehul Kothari of Anand Rathi recommends three shares to buy or sell
simplifiedContent: Mehul Kothari, an expert from Anand Rathi, has suggested three stocks that can be bought or sold. These stocks are IRB Infra, MMTC, and CESC, and they are all currently priced under ₹200. This means that investors can buy these stocks without having to spend a lot of money. Kothari's recommendations could be useful for investors who are looking to buy or sell stocks, as his advice is based on his expertise. Investors may want to consider these stocks as potential additions to their portfolio.
